name: AI Visibility Audit
cardBlurb: How a brand shows up in ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and AI Overviews — and which sources those answers cite instead of you. Outputs a prioritized GEO/AEO fix list.
tagline: Traditional SEO asks do we rank. This asks are we cited, and are we described correctly — across ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews. Different mechanics, different fixes.
description: A Claude skill that audits how a brand appears in ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and AI Overviews, then produces a prioritized GEO/AEO fix list. Free to fork.
problem: Rank tracking cannot see the surface that is eating your clicks. A brand can hold position three for its head term and still be absent from every AI answer that term now triggers.
The failure is almost never content volume. It is that the sources those answers cite do not mention you — so publishing more owned content moves nothing.
This skill measures presence, diagnoses which of five root causes is responsible, and returns a ranked fix list you can hand to someone on Monday.

steps.title: Build the prompt set
steps.body: 20–30 prompts across five intent tiers — discovery, comparison, problem-first, branded, and buying-criteria — weighted toward the unbranded questions where visibility is actually won.

steps.title: Run & record
steps.body: For each prompt: is the brand mentioned, where, described how — and crucially, which sources the answer cites. That citation column is where the fix lives.

steps.title: Diagnose the root cause
steps.body: Every gap maps to one of five causes: citation absence, entity ambiguity, extractability, comparative absence, or factual drift. Naming the cause is what makes the fix specific.

steps.title: Ship a ranked fix list
steps.body: Prioritized by (impact × confidence) ÷ effort, each item states what to do, why it moves AI visibility, who owns it, and how you'll know it worked. Re-measure in 60 days.

install: # 1. Clone the repo git clone https://github.com/seosdm/ai-visibility-audit.git # 2. Copy SKILL.md into a Claude Project, then prompt: Run the ai-visibility-audit skill for [brand]. Category: [what they sell]. Competitors: [3–5]. # 3. Re-run the same prompt set every 60 days to measure movement.
sampleVerdict: strong when named, near-invisible in discovery. Root cause — the three listicles cited across discovery prompts don't mention the brand. Highest-leverage move is earning placement in those sources, not publishing more owned content.
relatedBlurb: Where you're cited, and where you're not.

name: Screaming Frog Crawl Analysis
cardBlurb: Turns a 50,000-row crawl export into a causal technical diagnosis — indexability as a logic tree, true orphans, redirect chains, and internal link equity.
tagline: Screaming Frog gives you 40 columns and 50,000 rows. The skill is knowing which six columns answer which question — and how to cross-reference exports so the findings are causal, not just descriptive.
description: A Claude skill that turns a Screaming Frog export into a causal technical diagnosis — indexability, crawl depth, orphans and link equity. Free to fork.
problem: A list of "pages with missing titles" is a filter, not an audit. Anyone can sort a column. The value is in knowing which finding causes the others.
A noindexed page with a missing title tag does not have a title-tag problem. Resolve indexability as a logic tree and report the first failing gate — everything downstream is noise.

And prioritization is only credible when findings are weighted by traffic and links. A broken canonical on a zero-traffic page is not a priority, and saying so out loud is what builds trust with a client.

steps.title: Parse, don't eyeball
steps.body: analyze_crawl.py handles the export's quirks — mixed encodings, the header row, Address as key — and returns a structured summary to reason about rather than a raw table to squint at.

steps.title: Resolve indexability as a gate sequence
steps.body: Status 200 → robots directive → canonical → robots.txt → internally reachable → in sitemap. Report "fails at gate N", never a pile of independent flags.

steps.title: Run the five analyses that matter
steps.body: Crawl depth, true orphans (traffic or links but zero inlinks), redirect chains resolved to final destination, internal link equity per URL, and duplicate clusters diagnosed as patterns rather than 400 pasted rows.

steps.title: Weight, rank, and hand over
steps.body: Every finding carries scale, evidence, and business weight. Output includes a dev-ready redirect remediation list and specific internal linking actions — link these money pages from those authority pages.

install: # 1. Clone the bundle git clone https://github.com/seosdm/seo-skills.git cd seo-skills # 2. Export internal_all.csv from Screaming Frog (add all_inlinks.csv if you can) python skills/screaming-frog-crawl-analysis/scripts/analyze_crawl.py \ internal_all.csv --inlinks all_inlinks.csv # 3. Copy skills/screaming-frog-crawl-analysis/SKILL.md into a Claude Project: Run screaming-frog-crawl-analysis on this export. GSC data attached for weighting.
sampleVerdict: faceted navigation on /shop/* is generating 1,204 self-conflicting canonicals — one templating bug, not 1,204 problems. Fixing it recovers 39% of the crawl. The 27 true orphans carry backlinks and are the second move, not the first.
ctaLabel: Get This Run On Your Site
relatedBlurb: The technical floor everything else stands on.

name: GSC Opportunity Mining
cardBlurb: Striking-distance keywords, CTR underperformance, cannibalization, and page decay — mined from the only dataset that tells you what Google already thinks you're relevant for.
tagline: Search Console is the only dataset that tells you what Google already thinks you're relevant for. The fastest organic wins almost always live in queries you already rank 5–15 for.
description: A Claude skill that mines Search Console for striking-distance keywords, CTR gaps, cannibalization and page decay. Free to fork.
problem: Most audits reach for a third-party keyword tool and ignore the one dataset that reflects reality. Meanwhile page-one-adjacent queries sit there, already earning impressions, needing a title tag rather than a new article.
The bigger miss is decay. A single-period report physically cannot see it — and what you're losing is usually more urgent than what you could gain.
This skill always pulls two periods, separates seasonal from algorithmic from genuine decay, and refuses to recommend new content when the win is fixing a page that already ranks sixth.

steps.title: Pull two periods, always
steps.body: Via the connected GSC source or a Performance CSV — query and page level, with position, impressions, clicks and CTR, plus the prior comparable period so decay is computable.

steps.title: Mine striking distance
steps.body: Queries at average position 5–15 with real impressions, ranked by impressions × (1 − current CTR). Then segment: is the ranking URL the right URL? If not it's a mapping fix, not a content fix.

steps.title: Find the same-day wins
steps.body: Compare actual CTR to the expected curve for each position. Ranking well below it means a title/meta problem or someone owning the snippet above you — fixable this afternoon, no content work.

steps.title: Diagnose cannibalization and decay
steps.body: Group queries where multiple URLs draw impressions, flag flip-flopping, and classify every declining page as seasonal, algorithmic, or decaying. Mislabeling this wastes months.

install: # 1. Clone the bundle git clone https://github.com/seosdm/seo-skills.git # 2. Connect GSC, or export Queries + Pages from the GSC UI (16 months if offered) # 3. Copy skills/gsc-opportunity-mining/SKILL.md into a Claude Project: Run gsc-opportunity-mining for [property]. Last 3 months vs prior period.
sampleVerdict: the headline is the decay, not the upside. Nine pages lost 24% of clicks on one date — a broad algorithmic drop, not stale content, so rewriting them would have wasted a quarter. The 38 CTR gaps are title-tag edits worth more than any new article on the roadmap.
relatedBlurb: Where you already rank, and the cheapest wins.

name: Backlink & Keyword Gap
cardBlurb: Link velocity, anchor risk, reclamation, and the referring-domain gap — turned into a sequenced roadmap instead of "build more links".
tagline: "Build more links" is not a strategy. "These 12 referring domains link to all three competitors and none to you" is — and it comes with names, not adjectives.
description: A Claude skill for backlink profile audits and competitor keyword-gap analysis — link velocity, anchor risk, reclamation, and a content roadmap. Free to fork.
problem: Link profiles get reported by raw count, which tells you almost nothing. Five hundred links from irrelevant low-authority domains are worth less than twenty relevant editorial ones.

Meanwhile the single most actionable output in link building — domains that already link to two or more competitors but not to you — almost never appears in the deck. They're pre-qualified and reachable. They're the list.

This skill is also deliberately conservative on disavow. Most toxic-link panic is unwarranted, Google ignores junk on its own, and disavowing good links does real damage. It will tell you plainly when the answer is don't.

steps.title: Pull client and competitors identically
steps.body: Referring domains, backlink profile, anchor distribution, organic keywords and gap data — through the same pull, so the comparison is apples-to-apples rather than two different snapshots.

steps.title: Read the profile's shape
steps.body: Velocity trend (a rising lost-link line is often the hidden cause of a slow decline), quality by authority tier and topical relevance, and anchor-text risk across branded / naked / generic / exact-match.

steps.title: Bank the reclamation wins
steps.body: Lost links worth chasing and unlinked brand mentions — both convert far faster than cold outreach. The skill drafts the outreach for the top targets rather than leaving you a list.

steps.title: Turn the gap into a roadmap
steps.body: Referring-domain gap ranked by how many competitors each links to, then keyword gaps clustered into pillars and supporting pieces, sequenced by (traffic potential × relevance) ÷ difficulty.

install: # 1. Clone the bundle git clone https://github.com/seosdm/seo-skills.git # 2. Connect Ahrefs, or export referring domains + anchors + keyword gap as CSV # 3. Copy skills/backlink-keyword-gap/SKILL.md into a Claude Project: Run backlink-keyword-gap for [domain] vs [competitor1], [competitor2], [competitor3].
sampleVerdict: twelve domains link to every competitor and not to you — that's the quarter's outreach list, already qualified. Separately, exact-match anchors at 31% is a footprint worth diluting. Nothing in the profile warrants a disavow file; the junk here is ordinary and Google is already ignoring it.
relatedBlurb: The referring-domain gap that feeds AI citations.

name: SEO Content Brief
cardBlurb: A brief is a contract with the writer. Intent read from the actual SERP, must-cover entities, real internal links, and word counts derived from what ranks.
tagline: A brief is a contract with the writer. If it doesn't constrain them, it isn't a brief — it's a suggestion. Every section here is specific enough that two writers would produce structurally similar articles.
description: A Claude skill that produces writer-ready SEO content briefs — SERP-derived intent, must-cover entities, verified internal links, and honest risk. Free to fork.
problem: Most briefs are a keyword and a word count. The writer fills the gap with judgment they were never given, and the result fights the SERP.
If every result for a term is a listicle, a narrative essay will not rank regardless of how good it is. Intent has to be read from the actual SERP, not assumed from the keyword.

The most valuable thing this skill does is occasionally talk you out of the page. A brief that says "update the existing URL" or "you cannot win this term, here's the longer-tail entry point" is worth more than one that dutifully specs a page nobody will find.

steps.title: Read the SERP, don't assume it
steps.body: Top 8 results: page type, title format, depth, freshness, domain profile. Classify intent, name the dominant format, and check whether there's an AI Overview and what it cites — that's your extractable-answer target.

steps.title: Decide whether the page should exist
steps.body: Does a page already target this? Can this domain realistically compete? Does it serve the business goal or just traffic? The answer becomes a Recommendation block at the top of the brief.

steps.title: Write the outline as instructions
steps.body: H1, then every H2 and H3 with a note on what belongs under it. Mark the section that answers the query directly and put it above the fold — that's what gets extracted into snippets and AI answers.

steps.title: Constrain the specs honestly
steps.body: Word count derived from the ranking set with the observed range stated. Internal links as verified real URLs, at least one to a money page. Plus two or three sentences on what would make this page fail.

install: # 1. Clone the bundle git clone https://github.com/seosdm/seo-skills.git # 2. Copy skills/seo-content-brief/SKILL.md into a Claude Project, then prompt: Run seo-content-brief. Keyword: [target]. Domain: [site]. Goal: rank / convert / support. # 3. Hand the output straight to the writer. That's the point.
sampleVerdict: commercial-investigation intent, and every ranking result is a comparison listicle — a narrative guide would not place here. Recommendation is to update the existing URL rather than publish new, because it already earns impressions for four of the secondary terms.
ctaLabel: Train My Team To Run This
relatedBlurb: Briefs built for extraction, not just ranking.

name: Local SEO & GBP Audit
cardBlurb: Category strategy, NAP consistency, review velocity and sentiment, grid-aware pack visibility, and the specific prominence gap to the profile beating you.
tagline: Local ranking is a different algorithm — relevance, distance and prominence, weighted heavily toward the profile and the review corpus rather than the website. The profile is the landing page for the map pack.
description: A Claude skill that audits a Google Business Profile — categories, NAP, review velocity and map-pack prominence. Free to fork.
problem: An SEO who treats the Business Profile as an afterthought loses local clients. Most of the ranking signal lives somewhere the website audit never looks.
The primary category is the single biggest lever and the one most businesses get wrong. A wrong primary caps everything else you might do.

And a single-point rank check is misleading for local — a profile can rank first at the storefront and vanish two miles away. This skill states that caveat every time rather than quietly reporting one number.

steps.title: Fix the category first
steps.body: Check the primary against what the current pack occupants use for the target term, then recommend it plus every relevant secondary. Nothing else matters until this is right.

steps.title: Standardize NAP to byte-identical
steps.body: Name, address and phone across the profile, the website and major citations. Suite vs Ste, (416) vs 416 — each inconsistency fragments prominence. Output is the canonical version plus every deviation by source.

steps.title: Read reviews as data, not a score
steps.body: Velocity and recency against competitors, owner-response rate, and sentiment themes mined from the text — free voice-of-customer material that feeds content and CRO, not just a star average.

steps.title: Name the prominence gap
steps.body: "They hold 340 reviews at 4.8 adding 20 a month; you have 60 at 4.6 adding 2" is an actionable gap. Ends in a 90-day plan that separates profile work from website work from review work.

install: # 1. Clone the bundle git clone https://github.com/seosdm/seo-skills.git # 2. Copy skills/local-seo-gbp-audit/SKILL.md into a Claude Project, then prompt: Run local-seo-gbp-audit for [business], [city]. Target terms: [3–5]. Pack competitors: [3–5]. # 3. Spot-check rank from several points, not one. The skill will insist.
sampleVerdict: the primary category doesn't match what any pack occupant uses for the target term — that single change gates everything else, so it goes first and alone. Review velocity is the structural gap after that: ten times behind the leader, which no amount of on-site work compensates for.
relatedBlurb: The map pack runs on a different algorithm.

name: CRO Page Teardown
cardBlurb: Friction mapped to funnel stage, hypotheses with stated mechanisms, and a queue split into just-do-it, test-it, and research-it.
tagline: Opinions about button colours are worthless. This produces hypotheses tied to a specific friction, with a stated mechanism and a way to measure it — and it won't recommend a test your traffic can't support.
description: A Claude skill that runs a structured conversion teardown — friction map, ranked hypotheses, prioritized test queue. Free to fork.
problem: Most page feedback is a list of preferences dressed as expertise. "Make the CTA bigger" has no mechanism, so it can't be right or wrong — it just ships and nothing changes.

Worse, most teams A/B test at volumes that cannot resolve the difference. Under roughly a thousand conversions a month, testing is theatre; sequential changes and five user interviews will teach you more.
And frequently the page isn't the problem. If the real constraint is the offer or the traffic quality, this skill says that first, before anything else. Most "CRO problems" are targeting problems.

steps.title: Read the page as a visitor does
steps.body: The five-second test from above the fold alone: what is this, who is it for, why this one, what do I do next. If any is unanswerable that's finding #1 and it outranks everything else on the page.

steps.title: Map friction to funnel stage
steps.body: Every finding is classified attention, motivation, anxiety, or friction. These have different fixes, and anxiety and friction problems are usually far cheaper wins than motivation problems.

steps.title: Write hypotheses with mechanisms
steps.body: "Because [evidence], [segment] is [stage problem]. Changing X to Y should increase [metric] because [mechanism]." Any hypothesis without a stateable mechanism is rejected, not softened.

steps.title: Split the queue three ways
steps.body: Just do it (high confidence, low effort, no test needed), test it (real uncertainty and enough traffic, with MDE and runtime), and research it — naming the method and the exact question to ask.

install: # 1. Clone the repo git clone https://github.com/seosdm/cro-page-teardown.git # 2. Copy SKILL.md into a Claude Project, then prompt: Run cro-page-teardown on [url]. Conversion action: [x]. Traffic source: [y]. ~[n] conversions/month. # 3. Try it on your own homepage first. It will not be gentle.
sampleVerdict: the page fails the five-second test on "why this one" — four unfalsifiable claims above the fold and no proof adjacent to the ask. At 340 conversions a month there isn't traffic to A/B test this, so the queue is sequential: fix the six anxiety findings first, then run five interviews before touching the offer.
relatedBlurb: Ranking is worthless if the page doesn't convert.

name: Agency Ops · ClickUp
cardBlurb: Turns a ClickUp workspace into a weekly delivery report — account health, capacity bottlenecks, stalled work grouped by cause, and seven ranked actions.
tagline: At 5–20 accounts the failure mode isn't bad work — it's silent drift on one client while attention sits on another. This surfaces the drift, with the chase emails already written.
description: A Claude skill that turns a ClickUp workspace into a weekly agency delivery and pipeline health report. Free to fork.
problem: Agency status reports measure the wrong thing. Tasks are closing, everything's green, and meanwhile one account hasn't seen a client-facing deliverable in five weeks.

Closing internal tasks while producing nothing the client can feel is the classic agency failure, so this skill will never mark an account green on throughput alone. Silence precedes churn — days since last contact is a first-class signal here.
It's also deliberately strict. A report where everything is green is a report nobody reads twice.

steps.title: Score every account on six signals
steps.body: Throughput over 14 days, oldest untouched task, overdue vs no-due-date, unassigned work, days since last client-facing deliverable, days since last contact. Green, Amber, or Red — two breaches or 30 days without output is Red.

steps.title: Find the capacity bottleneck
steps.body: Open tasks, overdue count and tracked hours per person. Anyone carrying 30% above the team median is where the next missed deadline comes from. If one person blocks three Red accounts, that's structural, and the report says so.

steps.title: Group stalled work by cause
steps.body: Everything untouched over 21 days sorted into blocked-on-client, blocked-internally, scope creep, or genuinely forgotten. Most agency chaos is the first and third masquerading as a capacity problem.

steps.title: Cap the actions at seven
steps.body: Ranked, each with an owner and a day, opening with a single-sentence "the one thing". Chase emails for client-blocked items come pre-drafted — the report should reduce work, not create it.

install: # 1. Clone the repo git clone https://github.com/seosdm/agency-ops-clickup.git # 2. Connect ClickUp (or export tasks to CSV), then prompt: Run the weekly agency-ops-clickup report. Workspace: [name]. Week of [date]. # 3. Run it the same morning every week. The trend is the product.
sampleVerdict: both Red accounts trace to the same person, who is also carrying 40% above the team median — that's a structural problem, not a productivity one, and no amount of chasing fixes it. Nine of the fourteen stalled tasks are blocked on clients; the chase emails are drafted and attached.
relatedBlurb: The orchestration layer that runs the rest on schedule.
